transcript.text: the door on our built in dishwasher just crashes down when you open it now, used to stay put. Hotpoint I think

A dishwasher door that crashes down usually means the mechanism that holds it up has worn out. In most dishwashers, this is caused by worn balance springs or a failing hinge cable inside the top hinge assembly. Before we look at parts, let's rule out simple installation issues:
1. Check for obstructions: Make sure no cutlery basket or tall item in the racks is sticking out and preventing the door from closing fully.
2. Check alignment: Since it’s built-in, ensure the cabinet doors aren't rubbing against each other or the dishwasher frame when opening. To pinpoint the fault, could you tell me:
• When you open the door, does it feel heavy or stiff before it drops, or is it light and just falls?
• Does it physically latch (click) into place when you push it closed firmly?
It just falls, hardly any resistance on the right side, the left still has a bit of tension. It does close and latch fine though. Heard a twang noise last week when it went.

That 'twang' and the fact that only one side has lost tension suggests a mechanical failure in the door support system. In most dishwashers, including Hotpoint models, each hinge contains a cable or spring mechanism to hold the door up as you open it. The right-hand assembly has snapped or slipped, which is why it crashes down. This is not something that can be fixed by adjustment; the faulty part needs replacing. Safety first: ensure the dishwasher is switched off and isolated from the mains before doing any work. Replacing this usually involves removing the inner door panel or the top hinge cover to access the mechanism. If you are comfortable with basic DIY, I can guide you through finding the specific part number for your model. Do you have the full model number (usually on a sticker inside the door frame or on the side of the tub)?
Only partly, the sticker on the door edge is half peeled off but I can see it starts LTF. I looked under the plinth with a torch and can see a loose spring hanging down on the right side.

That suggests it. This is a common wear item on built-in dishwashers; the springs or cables inside the hinge assembly fatigue over time and eventually break. Because this involves removing parts of the door assembly to access the internal hinge mechanism, it requires some dismantling. If you are comfortable using basic tools (screwdrivers) and following instructions carefully, I can guide you on how to find the correct replacement part for your Hotpoint model (using that LTF number). However, if you would prefer not to dismantle the door yourself, this is a job for an engineer. The repair usually involves replacing both the left and right hinge assemblies (or at least the broken one) to ensure the door remains balanced. Would you like help finding the part number so you can order it, or do you need advice on finding a local engineer?
I can't pull the machine out to get at it, it's screwed to the worktop and the plinth is tight. Can you help me find the part? I only have the partial LTF 8B019 off the sticker.

[Heading: Likely cause: door hinge]
I can't confirm the exact part number for model LTF8B019 as it doesn't match a standard full Hotpoint code in my database. This repair requires dismantling the door assembly which is difficult without access to the rear. I recommend contacting an engineer or checking with a manufacturer-authorized spares dealer using the full model number from the remaining part of the sticker.
